holidays.name: National Cupcake Day
holidays.description: A sugary celebration of the frosted miniature cake. Bakers and sweet tooths alike are encouraged to whip up a batch, buy a box, or sneak one into the office break room.
holidays.origin: Cupcake Day is an unofficial American food observance that grew out of the cupcake boom of the 2000s, when bakeries dedicated solely to cupcakes began popping up across the country.
holidays.funFact: The word 'cupcake' was first recorded in 1828 in a recipe by Eliza Leslie, and early versions were baked in cups, which is how they got their name.

holidays.name: Bill of Rights Day
holidays.description: A day when Americans commemorate the ratification of the first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution, which guarantee freedoms like speech, religion, and the right to a fair trial.
holidays.origin: The Bill of Rights was ratified on December 15, 1791, when Virginia became the final state needed to approve it. President Franklin D. Roosevelt proclaimed the first Bill of Rights Day in 1941 for the 150th anniversary.
holidays.funFact: Of the twelve amendments originally proposed, only ten were ratified at first. One of the leftovers, about congressional pay raises, was finally ratified as the 27th Amendment in 1992, over 200 years later.

holidays.name: International Tea Day
holidays.description: A day for tea lovers around the world to steep, sip, and celebrate their favorite brew, from delicate green teas to a strong builder's cuppa.
holidays.origin: International Tea Day has been observed on December 15 by tea-producing countries such as India, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh, and was promoted by trade unions and tea growers to raise awareness of the interests of tea workers and producers. The UN later established its own International Tea Day on May 21.
holidays.funFact: Tea is the most consumed beverage in the world after water, and legend says it was discovered in 2737 BC when tea leaves blew into Emperor Shennong's pot of boiling water.

holidays.name: Za Za Zsa Gabor Day
holidays.description: A glitzy, glamorous day honoring the dazzling Hungarian-American actress and socialite known for her many marriages, her love of diamonds, and her signature 'dahling' catchphrase.
holidays.origin: Zsa Zsa Gabor was born on February 6, but the day is often noted among quirky calendars on December 18, the day she died in 2016; some lists place celebrations on or near the middle of December as a nod to her sparkling life of Hollywood excess.
holidays.funFact: Zsa Zsa Gabor was famously married nine times, and she once quipped that she was an excellent housekeeper because every time she got divorced, she kept the house.

holidays.name: Hanukkah-Era Wear a Funny Holiday Sweater Day
holidays.description: A cheerful day devoted to pulling out the loudest, tackiest, most blinking holiday sweater you own and wearing it with absolute pride.
holidays.origin: The ugly sweater tradition began with 1980s family sitcoms and holiday parties, and exploded into a full-blown cultural phenomenon in the 2010s. Mid-December is the peak season for sweater parties and charity events.
holidays.funFact: Some ugly sweaters are now made with built-in lights, jingle bells, and even tiny working speakers that play carols.
